previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and GERD, was admitted for acute shortness of breath due to decompensated heart failure. He presented with significant fluid overload, weight gain from 136.3 kg to 144 kg, pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, and a markedly elevated BNP of 8196. The exacerbation was attributed to dietary noncompliance, including high-sodium food intake, and partial noncompliance with hydralazine. He was treated with IV furosemide and supportive care, with gradual improvement in symptoms and weight reduction to 140.6 kg. An echocardiogram showed reduced ejection fraction of 25%. Concerns about diuretic use and kidney function were addressed through education and a family meeting. He was discharged home with optimized medical therapy, instructions for daily weight monitoring, and plans for follow-up labs and cardiology visit.
